Solve u_t = 0.05*(u_xx + u_yy) on x in [0,1], y in [0,1), t in [0, 0.3].
Use a tensor grid with Nx=60 intervals in x (61 points including both Dirichlet boundaries, dx=1/60) and Ny=64 periodic points in y on [0,1) (dy=1/64).
Apply 2nd-order central differences in both spatial directions, with Dirichlet ghost handling at x=0 and x=1 (u=0) and periodic wrap-around in y.
Integrate in time using Implicit Euler with dt=0.001 for exactly 300 steps (k=1 to 300), so that t reaches T=0.300.
At each implicit Euler step, assemble and solve the linear system (I - dt*0.05*L) u^{k+1} = u^k, where L is the 2D Laplacian operator with the described boundary treatments.
Initialize with u(x,y,0) = sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y).
The exact solution for verification is u_exact(x,y,t) = exp(-0.05*(pi**2 + (2*pi)**2)*t) * sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y).
Save the file "solution_agent_heat_16.npz" containing arrays x (1D, length 61), y (1D, length 64), u (2D, shape (64,61) so that u[j,i] = u(x[i], y[j]) at T=0.3), and scalar metadata T, dx, dy, dt.
Save a heatmap or contour plot of u(x,y,T=0.3) as "solution_agent_heat_16.png".
Print min(u), max(u), and the discrete L2 norm sqrt(sum(u**2)*dx*dy) at T.
Evaluate the exact solution on the same grid at T=0.3 and print the max absolute error and the discrete L2 error sqrt(sum((u-u_exact)**2)*dx*dy).
